decision.explanation: The right angle is at C, so tan(63°)=(3x+2)/(3x). Thus 3x=2/(tan(63°)-1)≈2.0777 and 3x+2≈4.0777. The area is (1/2)(2.0777)(4.0777)≈4.2362, which rounds to 4.2 square units.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13987450/assets/7dc806c646f1e9f5edbfef789fbdc9dfca2745c637906bd61eccb8072440e8c0.png)

In square units rounded to one decimal place, find the area of $△ABC$ shown above.
after.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={63}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘}) & =\frac{3x+2}{3x} \\ 3x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘}) & =3x+2 \\ 3x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-3x & =2 \\ 3x(\operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-1) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{3(\operatorname{tan}⁡({63}^{∘})-1)} \\ x & =0.692\,5…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x+2=3(0.692\,5…)+2=4.077\,6…, \\ AC & =3x=3(0.692\,5…)=2.077\,6….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(2.077\,6…)(4.077\,6…) \\  & =4.236\,0… \\  & ≈4.2,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the one decimal place.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({45}^{∘}) & =\frac{5x+5}{6x} \\ 1 & =\frac{5x+5}{6x} \\ 6x & =5x+5 \\ x & =5\end{aligned}

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =6x=6(5)=30, \\ BC & =5x+5=5(5)+5=30.\end{aligned}

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 30\cdot 30 \\  & =450.\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Determining the Area of a Triangle Given a Trigonometric Ratio of an Angle and the Length of a Leg

history.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{12}{13},$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the cosine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{12}{13} & =\frac{12}{AB} \\ AB & =\frac{12}{12}\cdot 13 \\ AB & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the missing side $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{13}^{2}-{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169-144} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 12 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$
